title: EmberPoint retail integration capture
content:
Customer: EmberPoint (regional retail chain, ~120 stores).
Context: Intro call 2024-10-15 with EmberPoint infra + analytics lead. They want to pilot LLM-powered cashier assistant + automated returns triage using Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated. Preference for Private due to PCI/data concerns, but open to hybrid.
Attendees: Ava M (Redwood SE), Liam O'C (Redwood), Priya S (Redwood Solutions PM), Jordan Patel (EmberPoint Head of Platform), Maria Gomez (EmberPoint Retail Ops), Dev Lead: Tyler Nguyen.
Call notes (raw):
- Primary goal: reduce average handling time for returns and improve front-line agent accuracy when responding to edge-case return reasons.
- Data flow they envision: POS event -> internal service enrich -> Redwood inference for assistant -> decision/action OR recommended message to cashier UI.
- Regulatory: cardholder data may be present in raw POS log; they WILL tokenize before sending but need guidance on PII minimization and KMS integration.
- Ops constraints: stores have variable connectivity; some branches behind proxy with strict egress rules.
- Latency SLO: 200ms p95 for single-turn assistant replies; batch scoring (end-of-day analytics) can be minutes.
- Throughput: expected peak 60 concurrent sessions per store during holiday (they want headroom). For pilot: target 10 stores, ~600 concurrent sessions peak -> estimate concurrency ~600.
- Data residency: want EU region for EM stores, NA for US.
- Budget: <$30k/mo initially for pilot (incl infra).
- Security: must support customer-managed KMS + audit logs + optional HSM for keys.
- Model concerns: they want to use an open model variant (weight-pin) but accept Redwood curated quantized flavor if we can guarantee parity.

Non-functional requirements (notes):
- Auth: OAuth2 token per store + service account for central ingestion.
- Network: allowlist Redwood control-plane IPs OR VPN peering to avoid opening broad egress. Must support private endpoints (VPC).
- Storage: logs to S3 (encrypted SSE-KMS), 30-day retention for debug, moving to cold storage at 90d.
- Observability: per-request tracing id injected into response so they can tie back to POS event. Need request-level cost metrics.
- Rollout: canary on 2 stores -> ramp to 10 -> full pilot.

Integration gotchas / risks:
- Proxy / TLS interception in some stores may break TLS pinning; need guidance and fallback to Dedicated in those sites. (Action: get sample proxy headers from EmberPoint network team).
- KV/cache size: their conversational flows include long receipts (~2–3k tokens). KV cache eviction and chunking required. Suggest enabling prefix caching and truncate receipts with heuristics (line items priority).
- Tokenization/PII: their POS events sometimes include suffix card PAN fragments (last 4) + internal customer notes with SSNs (rare). Recommend server-side scrubber prior to sending; offer redact helper snippets.
- Model hallucination tolerance: for returns we need conservative answers. Recommend retrieval-augmented responses and confidence threshold to fallback-to-human.

Proposed Redwood config (initial pilot):
- Deployment: Private deployment in customer AWS account (VPC) for NA stores; Redwood control plane access restricted via peering + IAM role.
- Model: open-llama-ensemble-v1 quantized 4-bit (subject to QA). Fallback: smaller fast quantized variant for overloaded capacity.
- Instance profile: reserved Dedicated pool of 8x A10G (or mix with A100 burst) for peak, autoscale disabled for pilot, manual scale windows.
- Networking: site-to-cloud via VPN peering + NAT restriction list. Provide instructions for corporate proxy exceptions.
- KMS: integrate with EmberPoint KMS key alias (customer-managed). Ensure logs redact key material.

Metrics & cost estimate (rough back-of-envelope):
- Average tokens per interaction: 350 (input+output).
- Pilot TPS target: 10 qps sustained, 600 concurrency peaks -> need batching + stream to meet 200ms p95.
- Estimated monthly cost: ~$18k–26k depending on quantization and batching effectiveness.

Open questions / follow-ups (to capture ASAP):
- Jordan: can you share a sanitized sample POS payload (remove PANs) and typical receipt lengths? (Ava)
- Tyler: confirm whether branch proxies perform TLS MITM (vendor and firmware). (Liam)
- Security: what is EmberPoint's KMS vendor? HSM requirement level? (Priya)
- Regional separation: confirm count of EU stores and preferred AWS region. (Ava)

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Provide pilot SOW outline + cost breakdown (Ava) - target 2024-10-18.
- Generate sample redact + preprocessor Python snippet for them to drop into ingestion pipeline (Liam) - target 2024-10-17.
- Run quick latency demo with sample POS snippet on Redwood hosted API to benchmark base latency (Priya/Liam) - do this by 2024-10-22.
- Create JIRA ticket for Private deployment onboarding (JIRA-ENG-4872) and link to this doc (Ava).

Hand-off checklist for onboarding engineer (notes to self):
- Ask for sanitized dataset (S3 share) + IAM read role.
- Confirm VPC CIDR overlap (if peering). If overlap present, plan for VPN NAT.
- Validate KMS key alias and IAM principal.
- Preload common return reasons into retrieval DB (approx 7–10k rows).
- Create canary plan: 2 stores -> metric gates: p95 latency <250ms, error rate <1%, human fallback <=5%.

Loose ideas / brainstorm (scratch):
- Could ship a lightweight edge inference module later for extremely low-connectivity stores (tiny reranker locally + call back to cloud for long-horizon context).
- Consider receipts fingerprinting to reduce token sizes: hash line items, keep counts + item categories.

Notes-to-self / friction log:
- EmberPoint is cost-sensitive; emphasize batching/hits-per-second savings in slides.
- Their infra lead prefers architecture diagrams over bullet lists. Prepare a one-pager.

-- end --
